### Templates API Source: https://resend.com/docs/knowledge-base/how-do-i-avoid-conflicting-with-my-mx-records Endpoints for managing email templates, including listing, creating, updating, deleting, publishing, and duplicating templates. ```APIDOC ## GET /templates ### Description Retrieves a list of all available email templates. ### Method GET ### Endpoint /templates ## PATCH /templates/:template_id ### Description Updates an existing email template. ### Method PATCH ### Endpoint /templates/:template_id ### Parameters #### Path Parameters - **template_id** (string) - Required - The ID of the template to update. ## DELETE /templates/:template_id ### Description Deletes a specified email template. ### Method DELETE ### Endpoint /templates/:template_id ### Parameters #### Path Parameters - **template_id** (string) - Required - The ID of the template to delete. ## POST /templates/:template_id/publish ### Description Publishes a specified email template. ### Method POST ### Endpoint /templates/:template_id/publish ### Parameters #### Path Parameters - **template_id** (string) - Required - The ID of the template to publish. ## POST /templates/:template_id/duplicate ### Description Duplicates a specified email template. ### Method POST ### Endpoint /templates/:template_id/duplicate ### Parameters #### Path Parameters - **template_id** (string) - Required - The ID of the template to duplicate. ``` -------------------------------- ### Create a Template via API Source: https://resend.com/docs/dashboard/templates/introduction Programmatically create a new email template with a name, sender address, subject, HTML content, and variables. Variables can have fallback values. ```javascript import { Resend } from 'resend'; const resend = new Resend('re_xxxxxxxxx'); await resend.templates.create({ name: 'order-confirmation', from: 'Resend Store ', subject: 'Thanks for your order!', html: '

Name: {{{PRODUCT}}}

Total: {{{PRICE}}}

', variables: [ { key: 'PRODUCT', type: 'string', fallbackValue: 'item', }, { key: 'PRICE', type: 'number', fallbackValue: 20, }, ], }); ``` -------------------------------- ### Create Template with Custom Variables Source: https://resend.com/docs/llms-full.txt This example demonstrates how to create a new template and define custom variables using the Resend API. The `variables` array in the request payload allows you to specify the `key`, `type`, and an optional `fallbackValue` for each custom variable. ```APIDOC ## POST /templates ### Description Creates a new email template with specified HTML content and custom variables. ### Method POST ### Endpoint /templates ### Parameters #### Request Body - **name** (string) - Required - The name of the template. - **html** (string) - Required - The HTML content of the template. Custom variables are referenced using triple curly braces, e.g., `{{{VARIABLE_NAME}}}`. - **variables** (array) - Optional - An array of objects, where each object defines a custom variable. - **key** (string) - Required - The name of the variable. - **type** (string) - Required - The data type of the variable (e.g., 'string', 'number'). - **fallbackValue** (any) - Optional - The default value to use if the variable is not provided during email sending. ``` -------------------------------- ### Create Template Source: https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/templates/create-template This endpoint allows you to create a new email template. You can define the template's name, subject, and HTML content. Optional variables can also be included. ```APIDOC ## POST /templates ### Description Creates a new email template with a specified name, subject, and content. You can also define optional variables for dynamic content. ### Method POST ### Endpoint /templates ### Request Body - **name** (string) - Required - The name of the template. - **subject** (string) - Required - The subject line of the email. - **html** (string) - Required - The HTML content of the template. - **text** (string) - Optional - The plain text content of the template. ### Request Example ```json { "name": "welcome_email", "subject": "Welcome to Our Service!", "html": "

Hi {{name}},

Welcome aboard!

", "text": "Hi {{name}}, Welcome aboard!" } ``` ### Response #### Success Response (200) - **id** (string) - The unique identifier of the created template. - **name** (string) - The name of the template. - **subject** (string) - The subject line of the template. - **html** (string) - The HTML content of the template. - **text** (string) - The plain text content of the template. - **created_at** (string) - The timestamp when the template was created. #### Response Example ```json { "id": "tpl_abc123xyz", "name": "welcome_email", "subject": "Welcome to Our Service!", "html": "

Hi {{name}},

Welcome aboard!

", "text": "Hi {{name}}, Welcome aboard!", "created_at": "2023-10-27T10:00:00Z" } ``` ``` -------------------------------- ### Templates API Source: https://resend.com/docs/dashboard/topics/introduction Manage your email templates with the Resend API. You can list, create, update, delete, publish, and duplicate templates. ```APIDOC ## List Templates ### Description Retrieves a list of all your templates. ### Method GET ### Endpoint /templates ### Response #### Success Response (200) - **data** (array) - A list of template objects. - **next_cursor** (string) - Cursor for the next page of results. - **has_more** (boolean) - Indicates if there are more results. ### Response Example ```json { "data": [ { "id": "tpl_abc123", "name": "Welcome Email", "created_at": "2023-10-26T10:00:00Z", "updated_at": "2023-10-26T10:00:00Z" } ], "next_cursor": "some_cursor", "has_more": true } ``` ``` ```APIDOC ## Update Template ### Description Updates an existing template. ### Method PATCH ### Endpoint /templates/:template_id ### Parameters #### Path Parameters - **template_id** (string) - Required - The ID of the template to update. ### Request Body - **name** (string) - Optional - The new name for the template. - **subject** (string) - Optional - The new subject for the template. - **html** (string) - Optional - The new HTML content for the template. - **plaintext** (string) - Optional - The new plaintext content for the template. ### Request Example ```json { "name": "Updated Welcome Email", "subject": "Welcome to Our Service!" } ``` ### Response #### Success Response (200) - **id** (string) - The ID of the updated template. - **name** (string) - The name of the updated template. - **subject** (string) - The subject of the updated template. - **html** (string) - The HTML content of the updated template. - **plaintext** (string) - The plaintext content of the updated template. - **created_at** (string) - The creation timestamp. - **updated_at** (string) - The last update timestamp. ### Response Example ```json { "id": "tpl_abc123", "name": "Updated Welcome Email", "subject": "Welcome to Our Service!", "html": "

Hello!

", "plaintext": "Hello!", "created_at": "2023-10-26T10:00:00Z", "updated_at": "2023-10-26T10:05:00Z" } ``` ``` ```APIDOC ## Delete Template ### Description Deletes a template. ### Method DELETE ### Endpoint /templates/:template_id ### Parameters #### Path Parameters - **template_id** (string) - Required - The ID of the template to delete. ### Response #### Success Response (200) - **id** (string) - The ID of the deleted template. ### Response Example ```json { "id": "tpl_abc123" } ``` ``` ```APIDOC ## Publish Template ### Description Publishes a template, making it available for use. ### Method POST ### Endpoint /templates/:template_id/publish ### Parameters #### Path Parameters - **template_id** (string) - Required - The ID of the template to publish. ### Response #### Success Response (200) - **id** (string) - The ID of the published template. - **published_at** (string) - The timestamp when the template was published. ### Response Example ```json { "id": "tpl_abc123", "published_at": "2023-10-26T10:10:00Z" } ``` ``` ```APIDOC ## Duplicate Template ### Description Creates a copy of an existing template. ### Method POST ### Endpoint /templates/:template_id/duplicate ### Parameters #### Path Parameters - **template_id** (string) - Required - The ID of the template to duplicate. ### Response #### Success Response (200) - **id** (string) - The ID of the newly duplicated template. - **name** (string) - The name of the duplicated template. ### Response Example ```json { "id": "tpl_xyz789", "name": "Welcome Email (Copy)" } ``` ```

### Send Email with Template

Source: https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/emails/send-email

This endpoint allows you to send emails using pre-defined templates. You can provide variables to customize the email content dynamically. If all required template variables are supplied, the email is sent. Otherwise, a validation error is returned.

```APIDOC
## POST /emails

### Description
Sends an email using a specified template and provided variables.

### Method
POST

### Endpoint
/emails

### Parameters
#### Request Body
- **from** (string) - Required - The sender's email address.
- **to** (string) - Required - The recipient's email address.
- **template_id** (string) - Required - The ID of the template to use.
- **variables** (object) - Required - A key/value object containing template variables.
  - **key** (string) - Required - The name of the variable. May only contain ASCII letters (a–z, A–Z), numbers (0–9), and underscores (_).

### Request Example
```json
{
  "from": "you@example.com",
  "to": "recipient@example.com",
  "template_id": "your_template_id",
  "variables": {
    "CTA": "Sign up now",
    "CTA_LINK": "https://example.com/signup"
  }
}
```

### Response
#### Success Response (200)
- **id** (string) - The unique identifier for the sent email.

#### Response Example
```json
{
  "id": "email_id_12345"
}
```
```

--------------------------------

### Send Email with Template

Source: https://resend.com/docs/llms-full.txt

Demonstrates how to send an email using a pre-defined template and variables via the Resend API.

```APIDOC
## POST /emails

### Description
Sends an email using a specified template and associated variables.

### Method
POST

### Endpoint
https://api.resend.com/emails

### Parameters
#### Request Body
- **from** (string) - Required - The sender's email address.
- **to** (string or array) - Required - The recipient's email address(es).
- **template** (object) - Required - The template to use for the email.
  - **id** (string) - Required - The ID of the template.
  - **variables** (object) - Optional - Key-value pairs for template variables.

### Request Example
```json
{
  "from": "Acme <onboarding@resend.dev>",
  "to": "delivered@resend.dev",
  "template": {
    "id": "order-confirmation",
    "variables": {
      "PRODUCT": "Vintage Macintosh",
      "PRICE": 499
    }
  }
}
```

### Response
#### Success Response (200)
- **id** (string) - The ID of the sent email.

#### Response Example
```json
{
  "id": "d030773c-0000-1000-0000-000000000000"
}
```
```

--------------------------------

### Send Email with Template

Source: https://resend.com/docs/dashboard/templates/introduction

Use this to send an email using a pre-defined template ID and pass custom variables for personalization. Ensure the template exists in your Resend dashboard.

```javascript
await resend.emails.send({
  from: 'Acme <onboarding@resend.dev>',
  to: 'delivered@resend.dev',
  template: {
    id: 'order-confirmation',
    variables: {
      PRODUCT: 'Vintage Macintosh',
      PRICE: 499,
    },
  },
});
```

--------------------------------

### Send Email with Template and Variables (Node.js)

Source: https://resend.com/docs/llms-full.txt

Use this snippet to send a transactional email using a published template ID and provide specific variable values for personalization. Ensure the Resend library is installed and initialized with your API key.

```typescript
import { Resend } from 'resend';

const resend = new Resend('re_xxxxxxxxx');

const { data, error } = await resend.emails.send({
  from: 'Acme <onboarding@resend.dev>',
  to: ['delivered@resend.dev'],
  subject: 'hello world',
  template: {
    id: 'f3b9756c-f4f4-44da-bc00-9f7903c8a83f',
    variables: {
      PRODUCT: 'Laptop',
    },
  },
});
```

### Send Batch Emails > Parameters > template

Source: https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/emails/send-batch-emails

To send an email using a template, provide a `template` object with the `id` (or alias) of the published template and an optional `variables` object for template-specific data. If a `template` is provided, you cannot include `html`, `text`, or `react` content in the same payload. Fields like `from`, `subject`, and `reply_to` in the payload will override the template's defaults if provided.

### Manage Email Templates Source: https://resend.com/docs/llms-full.txt Commands for creating, managing, and publishing email templates. Supports creation with React Email, listing, retrieval, updating, publishing drafts, duplicating, and deleting templates. ```bash resend templates create --name "Welcome" --subject "Welcome to Acme" --react-email ./emails/welcome.tsx ``` ```bash resend templates list # List all templates ``` ```bash resend templates get # Retrieve a template by ID or alias ``` ```bash resend templates update # Update a template ``` ```bash resend templates publish # Publish a draft template ``` ```bash resend templates duplicate # Duplicate a template ``` ```bash resend templates delete # Delete a template ``` ```bash resend templates open [id] # Open a template in the dashboard ``` -------------------------------- ### Create an Email Template using Resend CLI Source: https://resend.com/docs/cli Use this command to create a new email template. You can specify the name, subject, and content for the template. ```shellscript resend templates create --name "Welcome Email" --subject "Welcome to our service!" --html "

Hello {{name}},

Thank you for joining us.

" ``` -------------------------------- ### Update an Email Template using Resend CLI Source: https://resend.com/docs/cli Use this command to update an existing email template. You can modify its name, subject, or content. ```shellscript resend templates update --id "" --name "Updated Welcome Email" --subject "Welcome!" --html "

Hello {{name}},

We are glad to have you.

" ``` -------------------------------- ### Publish a Draft Template with CLI Source: https://resend.com/docs/cli Use this command to publish a draft email template. Provide the template ID to publish the draft. ```bash resend templates publish ``` -------------------------------- ### List All Email Templates using Resend CLI Source: https://resend.com/docs/cli This command lists all the email templates available in your Resend account. ```shellscript resend templates list # List all templates ```

### Set Resend API Key Environment Variable

Source: https://resend.com/docs/llms-full.txt

Export your Resend API key as an environment variable. This key is required for authentication.

```sh
export RESEND_API_KEY="re_xxxxxxxxx"
```

--------------------------------

### Resend CLI Authentication Priority

Source: https://resend.com/docs/cli

Illustrates the priority order for API key resolution in the Resend CLI. The CLI checks for the --api-key flag first, then the RESEND_API_KEY environment variable, and finally looks for saved credentials.

```text
1 (highest) flag --api-key resend --api-key re_xxx emails send ...
2 ENV var RESEND_API_KEY export RESEND_API_KEY=re_xxx
3 (lowest) Saved credentials resend login
```

--------------------------------

### GitHub Actions CI/CD Setup

Source: https://resend.com/docs/llms-full.txt

Configure GitHub Actions to use the RESEND_API_KEY environment variable for sending emails via the Resend CLI. This avoids the need for manual login.

```yaml
# GitHub Actions
env:
  RESEND_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.RESEND_API_KEY }}
steps:
  - run: |
      resend emails send \
        --from "Acme <onboarding@resend.dev>" \
        --to delivered@resend.dev \
        --subject "Deploy complete" \
        --text "Version ${{ github.sha }} deployed."
```

--------------------------------

### Authenticate with Resend CLI non-interactively

Source: https://resend.com/docs/llms-full.txt

In non-interactive environments like CI or pipes, use the `--key` flag with `resend login` to provide your API key.

```bash
resend login --key re_xxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

### CLI Authentication

Source: https://resend.com/docs/cli

The Resend CLI supports multiple ways to authenticate, with a clear order of precedence. The CLI first checks for an API key provided via the `--api-key` flag, then looks for the `RESEND_API_KEY` environment variable, and finally uses saved credentials from `resend login`. If no API key is found through any of these methods, the CLI will return an `auth_error`.

The default rate limit is 5 requests per second per team. Exceeding this limit will result in a 429 response error code.

## Rate limit

The default maximum rate limit is **5 requests per second per team**. This limit applies across all API keys associated with your team. This number can be increased for trusted senders by request. You can view your team's current rate limit on the [Settings Usage page](https://resend.com/settings/usage). After that, you'll hit the rate limit and receive a `429` response error code.

Source: https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/rate-limit

The Resend API includes specific headers in its responses to inform you about your current rate limits. These headers conform to the sixth IETF standard draft for rate limit headers.

```APIDOC
## Rate Limits

### Response Headers

The response headers describe your current rate limit following every request in conformance with the sixth IETF standard draft:

| Header name       | Description                                           |
|-------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| `ratelimit-limit` | Maximum number of requests allowed within a window.   |
| `ratelimit-remaining` | How many requests you have left within the current window. |
| `ratelimit-reset` | How many seconds until the limits are reset.          |
| `retry-after`     | How many seconds you should wait before making a follow-up request. |

The default maximum rate limit is **5 requests per second per team**. This limit applies across all API keys associated with your team. This number can be increased for trusted senders upon request.
```

Source: https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/templates/list-templates

### Description
Retrieves a list of all your email templates.

### Method
GET

### Endpoint
/templates

### Query Parameters
- **limit** (integer) - Optional - The number of templates to return per page. Defaults to 50.
- **after** (string) - Optional - Returns templates after a specific template ID (used for pagination).
- **before** (string) - Optional - Returns templates before a specific template ID (used for pagination).

--------------------------------

### Publish Template

Source: https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/templates/publish-template

Publishes an email template using the Resend API. Requires the template ID and a valid API key.

```javascript
const publishTemplate = async (templateId, apiKey) => {
  const response = await fetch('https://api.resend.com/templates/:template_id/publish', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${apiKey}`
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ template_id: templateId })
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    const errorData = await response.json();
    throw new Error(`Failed to publish template: ${errorData.message}`);
  }

  return await response.json();
};

// Example usage:
const apiKey = 'YOUR_API_KEY';
const templateId = 'YOUR_TEMPLATE_ID';

publishTemplate(templateId, apiKey)
  .then(data => console.log('Template published successfully:', data))
  .catch(error => console.error('Error:', error));
```

### Templates > Publish a Template

Source: https://resend.com/docs/llms-full.txt

Templates are in a draft state by default and must be published to be used for sending emails. Publishing can be done through the dashboard or the API. Once published, you can continue to edit the template, and changes are saved as drafts. These changes will only be reflected in emails after you publish the template again.

--------------------------------

### Templates > Version History > Draft vs Published

Source: https://resend.com/docs/dashboard/templates/version-history

Templates begin in a draft state and must be published to be used for sending emails. This draft vs. published separation enables thorough testing before going live, making changes without affecting active emails, and maintaining version control over email content. The published version is used for sending emails until a new version is published. Progress on a draft template is automatically saved and does not affect the published version.

--------------------------------

### Draft vs Published

Source: https://resend.com/docs/llms-full.txt

After publishing a template, you can continue to edit it in draft mode without affecting the live version. This allows for testing and validation of new changes before they are deployed.

I have everything I need. Here is the consolidated research summary. --- # Resend Templates — API & CLI Reference (2026) ## 1. The `resend` CLI — Templates subcommand **Yes**, the CLI manages dashboard-hosted Templates. Source: , . ### Subcommands ```bash resend templates create # Create a new template (starts as draft) resend templates list # List all templates resend templates get # Retrieve a template by ID or alias resend templates update resend templates publish # Publish a draft resend templates duplicate resend templates delete resend templates open [id] # Open in the dashboard ``` ### `templates create` flags (documented surface) ```bash resend templates create \ --name "Welcome" \ --subject "Welcome to Acme" \ --html "

Hi {{{NAME}}}

" \ --var PRODUCT:string:item \ --var PRICE:number:25 # OR (mutually exclusive with --html): --react-email ./emails/welcome.tsx ``` Flags explicitly documented for the CLI: `--name`, `--subject`, `--html` / `--react-email`, repeated `--var KEY:TYPE:FALLBACK`. **Not documented as CLI flags**: `--alias`, `--from`, `--reply-to`, `--text`, `--status` (draft/published), or a raw `--variables` JSON. The same restricted flag set applies to `templates update`. **Gotcha for the CI pipeline:** if you need `alias`, `from`, `reply_to`, `text`, or a non-string `fallbackValue`, the CLI's template surface is incomplete — fall back to the REST API (or the Node SDK) for full control. ### CLI authentication (auth precedence, highest first) 1. `--api-key re_xxx` flag on any command 2. `RESEND_API_KEY` environment variable 3. Saved credentials from `resend login [--key re_xxx]` Source: . CI-friendly setup: ```yaml env: RESEND_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.RESEND_API_KEY }} ``` --- ## 2. Resend REST Templates API (`https://api.resend.com`) All requests require `Authorization: Bearer re_xxxxxxxxx` and `Content-Type: application/json`. ### Create a template — `POST /templates` Source: Request body fields: | Field | Type | Required | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | `name` | string | yes | Human-readable name | | `html` | string | yes | HTML body. Variables referenced as `{{{VAR_NAME}}}` (triple-brace Handlebars) | | `from` | string | no | `"Your Name "`. Sets the default sender; can be overridden at send time | | `subject` | string | no | Default subject; overridable at send time | | `reply_to` | string \| string[] | no | Default reply-to; overridable | | `text` | string | no | Plain text body. If omitted, derived from `html`. Empty string opts out | | `alias` | string | no | **Stable string identifier usable at send time** (see §3) | | `variables` | array | no | Up to 50 entries; each `{ key, type, fallback_value }` | | `react` | `React.ReactNode` | no | Node.js SDK only — server-renders to HTML | Created templates are **drafts** by default — they cannot be used to send until published. Source: . ### Update a template — `PATCH /templates/:template_id` *(also shown as `PUT /templates/{id}` in some docs — see gotcha)* Source: . Path param `:template_id` accepts either the template UUID or the alias. All body fields are optional (sparse update): `name`, `html`, `alias`, `from`, `subject`, `reply_to`, `text`, `react`, `variables`. Updates land as **drafts** — they do not affect the live published version until you re-publish. ### Publish a template — `POST /templates/:template_id/publish` Source: . Empty body. Response: ```json { "id": "34a080c9-...", "object": "template" } ``` There is **no documented `unpublish` endpoint** — once published, you continue editing against a draft and re-publish to roll forward. ### Get a template — `GET /templates/:template_id` Path param accepts ID **or alias** (CLI confirms: `resend templates get `). Response fields (assembled from create/publish docs and SDK examples — the official `get-template` API reference is thin; the canonical full shape is what `list` and `create` return): ```json { "id": "d9d69002-6301-4a9e-8317-43717351079f", "name": "Welcome Email", "alias": "welcome-message", "status": "draft", // "draft" | "published" "from": "Acme ", "subject": "Welcome", "html": "

Hi {{{NAME}}}

", "text": "Hi {{NAME}}", "reply_to": ["reply@example.com"], "variables": [ { "key": "NAME", "type": "string", "fallback_value": "friend" } ], "created_at": "2026-10-06 23:47:56.678+00", "updated_at": "2026-10-06 23:47:56.678+00", "published_at": "2026-10-07 10:00:00.000Z" // present when published } ``` (`status` and `published_at` are documented on the publish response and version-history page; `alias` is documented on the list response.) ### List templates — `GET /templates` Source: . Pagination: cursor-based, query params: - `limit` (int, default 50) - `after` (string) — return templates after this template ID - `before` (string) — return templates before this template ID Response envelope: ```json { "object": "list", "data": [ { "id": "...", "name": "...", "alias": "...", "status": "...", "created_at": "...", "updated_at": "..." } ], "has_more": true, "next_cursor": "..." // some pages also return "next_page_token" } ``` (`has_more` + cursor field names vary slightly across doc snippets — `next_cursor` and `next_page_token` both appear.) ### Other endpoints - `DELETE /templates/:template_id` → `{ "id": "..." }` - `POST /templates/:template_id/duplicate` → `{ "id": "...", "name": "Original (Copy)" }` --- ## 3. Sending with an alias at send time **Yes** — `template.id` accepts either the template UUID **or the alias**. Source: , : > "To send an email using a template, provide a `template` object with an `id` (or alias) of the published template and an optional `variables` object." ```jsonc POST https://api.resend.com/emails { "from": "Acme ", "to": "delivered@resend.dev", "template": { "id": "order-confirmation", // <-- works with alias string "variables": { "PRODUCT": "Vintage Macintosh", "PRICE": 499 } } } ``` **Constraints at send time** (worth knowing for CI): - `template` cannot coexist with `html`, `text`, or `react` in the same payload. - Top-level `from`, `subject`, `reply_to` in the send payload **override** the template defaults. - Variable keys must match ASCII letters / digits / underscores only; missing variables with no `fallback_value` cause a validation error. Alias is **settable** on both `POST /templates` (create) and `PATCH /templates/:id` (update) — confirmed by the create-template and update-template reference pages (both list `alias` in the body parameters). --- ## 4. Rate limits & gotchas - **Default rate limit: 5 requests per second per team**, shared across all API keys for the team. Source: . Exceeding returns `429`. - Response headers (IETF draft-6): - `ratelimit-limit`, `ratelimit-remaining`, `ratelimit-reset`, `retry-after` - One older doc snippet also mentions "100 requests per minute per IP" — the **5 req/sec per team** is the current canonical value (rate-limit page); the 100/min/IP phrasing is legacy. - Limits can be raised on request for trusted senders (Settings → Usage page). - **HTTP method inconsistency**: the update-template reference shows `PUT /templates/{id}` while other Resend pages (knowledge-base, dashboard topics) show `PATCH /templates/:template_id`. The Node SDK example uses `resend.templates.update()` (which maps to `PATCH`). For CI, **prefer PATCH** as the safe default and fall back to PUT only if a 405 surfaces in your environment. --- ## 5. Source URLs (everything referenced above) - CLI overview: - CLI auth & `RESEND_API_KEY`: (section "CLI Authentication") - Templates dashboard intro: - Templates draft vs published: - API reference index: , `…/update-template`, `…/publish-template`, `…/list-templates`, `…/delete-template` - Send email (template via alias): , - Rate limits: - Full LLM-readable mirror: --- ## TL;DR for the CI sync pipeline - **CLI works** for create / update / publish / list / get / duplicate / delete, but its flag surface on `templates create`/`update` is narrow: `--name --subject --html|--react-email --var KEY:TYPE:FALLBACK`. No documented `--alias`, `--from`, `--reply-to`, `--text`, or `--status` flags. - **REST API** gives you the full surface: `POST /templates` with `{name, html, from?, subject?, reply_to?, text?, alias?, variables?, react?}`. Edit-as-draft, then `POST /templates/:id/publish`. Update via `PATCH /templates/:id` (alias-acceptable). - **Alias works as a stable send-time address**: `{ template: { id: "", variables: {…} } }` in `POST /emails`. - **Drafts must be published** before `POST /emails` will use them — write/upsert + explicit publish are two separate calls. - **5 req/sec/team** is the cap; respect `retry-after` on 429s. - **Auth:** `RESEND_API_KEY` env var (or `--api-key` flag, or `resend login --key`) — wire it as a CI secret. Given your stated needs (`alias`, `from`, `subject`, `html` from React Email), the cleanest CI path is **Node SDK `resend.templates.create(...)` / `update()` / `publish()`**, falling back to raw `fetch` to `api.resend.com` for anything the CLI can't express — not the CLI itself.
